findings.summary: The comment justifying the new rootGitignore input states a MEASUREMENT about a test that is not in this tree: 'FreshCheckoutTest asserts check-gate-scope refuses when .gitignore stops ignoring .tmp/. Measured: without this, removing that line left `test` UP-TO-DATE and the gate printed ok having not run the test that fails on exactly that edit.' FreshCheckoutTest as staged contains exactly one @Test, about .harness/ and check-harness-tests.sh; nothing in buildSrc/src asserts anything about check-gate-scope or about .tmp/ being ignored (grep for 'gitignore' and 'check-gate-scope' in buildSrc/src returns only comments). The declaration itself is defensible on a DIFFERENT and unstated ground -- freshCheckout() runs `git add -A` inside the fixture, which honours the copied .gitignore, so a new pattern matching a tracked path breaks the trackedIn(fixture)==trackedIn(source) post-condition -- but that is not what the comment says. AGENTS.md non-negotiable 4 makes an unearned 'Measured:' the one claim this project cannot carry. Secondary: inserting the block at line 50 orphaned the lines 41-45 comment ('three suites assert against the module list derived from settings.gradle.kts') from the settings.gradle.kts declaration it explains, which now sits at 53-55.
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer preparing M0.31 greps for the test the comment names, finds no assertion about check-gate-scope or about .tmp/ anywhere in buildSrc/src, concludes rootGitignore is a leftover from the reverted half and deletes it. The real dependency -- the fixture's `git add -A` honouring the copied .gitignore -- is undocumented, so the deletion looks safe. A later commit adds a .gitignore pattern matching a tracked path; Gradle reports the buildSrc test task UP-TO-DATE, check-harness-tests.sh prints 'ok N harness test(s) pass', and the fixture post-condition that would have caught it never runs. Independently, anyone verifying the 'Measured:' claim against this tree cannot reproduce it, because no staged test fails on that edit.

findings.summary: gate() carries a comment describing the removed half as delivered -- 'the personal ignore file, which decides check-gate-scope's answer: a developer whose ~/.config/git/ignore lists .tmp/ would make this test pass over a repository that had stopped ignoring it' -- and the two statements it justifies (lines 136-137) are byte-identical duplicates of what scrub(pb, dir) already set one line earlier (scrub sets HOME=home and XDG_CONFIG_HOME=home/xdg; gate passes dir as home). No code path in this file consults a personal ignore file for check-gate-scope any more. The javadoc's own account of the split is honest (it names M0.31 explicitly), which makes this comment the only place that still asserts the removed assertion exists.
findings.failure_scenario: The comment is the only documentation of why HOME/XDG are pinned. A maintainer deduplicating gate() reads it, sees it names a gate this class no longer invokes, deletes the duplicated puts AND the scrub() lines as dead, and the fixture's own `git add -A` in run() then honours the developer's ~/.config/git/ignore -- the environment deciding the answer in the test whose stated thesis is that it must not. On a machine with a personal ignore matching a tracked path the fixture post-condition fails; on every other machine it passes, so the breakage lands as a per-developer flake with no comment left to explain it.

findings.summary: Three residues of the reverted half in freshCheckout(). (a) The tar sanity anchor asserts scripts/check-gate-scope.sh exists -- an arbitrary file this commit does not touch -- where scripts/check-harness-tests.sh, the script actually under test, is the correct anchor. (b) Line 69 asserts .tmp/ does not exist with the message 'that is the point'; .tmp/ is not the point of any staged assertion, .harness/ on the next line is. (c) The symlink rationale is stated twice, nearly word for word, at 47-55 and again at 62-65 ('dropped the tracked SYMLINK .claude/skills silently -- a fixture that is not the checkout it claims to be, in a test about what a checkout looks like').
findings.failure_scenario: M0.31 renames or restructures check-gate-scope.sh; this test fails at line 57 with 'sanity: the tar copy must have produced the tree', pointing the reader at the tar pipeline rather than at the rename, in a test that has nothing to do with that script. The duplicated paragraph and the 'that is the point' message cost a future reader a round of reconciling two accounts that are the same account.

findings.summary: The M0.31 row ends 'Fixture and four tests are built and held'. Nothing in the tree holds them: buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/ contains no gate-scope fixture, git status shows no untracked or unstaged candidate, and the staged FreshCheckoutTest has one @Test. The rest of the row is accurate and genuinely valuable -- all three false greens including the negative-pattern case are recorded in prose, which is the part that survives -- but the closing sentence promises artifacts a future reader cannot locate. M0.29's row is correctly narrowed to the .harness/ mkdir and its State cell follows the M0.5 precedent of a done row in the live table.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever picks up M0.31 reads 'built and held', spends a session looking for the fixture in branches, stashes and .harness/, finds nothing because it lived only in a session that has ended, and either rebuilds it from the prose anyway or -- worse -- assumes the four tests exist somewhere and writes fewer.
